headline: Debris field found off Nantucket as Coast Guard searches for six aboard medical plane
dek: Searchers found debris linked to a Canadian-registered air ambulance that vanished Saturday on a Bermuda-to-Boston flight; the six people aboard remain unaccounted for.
body: Searchers found a debris field off Nantucket linked to the medical transport aircraft that vanished Saturday on a flight from Bermuda to Boston, the U.S. Coast Guard said, according to an [Associated Press report](https://apnews.com/article/plane-search-bermuda-boston-nantucket-ccb6014ac35e2af11879e28e6c8527df). The finding changes the search from a hunt for an aircraft with no known location to a recovery and rescue operation centered on wreckage south of the island. The six people aboard remained unaccounted for in the latest reports, and the Coast Guard said a cutter would continue searching overnight and into Sunday.

The aircraft was a Canadian-registered Gulfstream G100 traveling from L.F. Wade International Airport in Bermuda to Boston Logan International Airport. The Coast Guard’s Northeast District identified the flight and its six occupants in an [official update](https://x.com/USCGNortheast/status/2106332164568801317). The Federal Aviation Administration issued a search-and-rescue alert after losing contact early Saturday, while [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/medical-plane-missing-nantucket-six-on-board/) reported that the jet had departed around 11:40 p.m. Eastern time Friday and was expected at Logan about 1:30 a.m.

The people aboard have not been publicly identified. AP reported that four were Canadian nationals and two were Bermudian nationals, and that their next of kin had been notified. Bermuda airport operator Skyport said, according to AP, that the aircraft carried four crew members and two passengers. Those details establish the makeup of the flight but do not answer whether anyone survived or what happened after the plane lost contact.

The aircraft’s last known moments are also still under investigation. AP reported that air-traffic-control audio captured a controller asking whether the pilot was “coming in blind” as a storm approached, and that the pilot had reported electrical problems and declared an emergency. The pilot’s response was not audible in the recording. Preliminary flight-tracking data showed a sharp descent from roughly 24,000 feet to about 10,000 feet, but that change alone does not establish the aircraft’s condition, direction or cause of the disappearance.

The Coast Guard’s response has involved air and surface crews from across the region. Earlier reporting by [Boston 25 News](https://www.boston25news.com/news/local/coast-guard-searching-missing-medical-transfer-jet-bound-boston/DLHUFCDJ2FCMBESR4W3MIIOEFA/) identified an HC-144 Ocean Sentry aircraft, an MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter from Air Station Cape Cod, a 47-foot motor lifeboat from Station Brant Point on Nantucket and the cutter William Sparling. [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/03/nx-s1-5597878/coast-guard-searching-for-missing-medical-plane-carrying-6-people) reported that an HC-130 Hercules aircraft also joined the effort.

The debris discovery does not by itself establish the full crash sequence or a final casualty count. The Coast Guard’s continuing search is aimed at locating people and additional aircraft evidence, while investigators will need to determine why the jet lost contact and descended. The National Transportation Safety Board told AP it was gathering information, and Canada’s transport minister said his government was monitoring the response. Nantucket, Cape Cod and Boston remain connected to the operation because the aircraft was headed to Logan and the search area is close to the island’s southern waters.

For residents watching from shore, the confirmed update is narrower than the many unanswered questions circulating online: debris has been found, six people are still unaccounted for, and the Coast Guard continues to search. Officials have not released the names of those aboard, the medical circumstances of the flight or a cause. Those facts should remain separate from preliminary audio, flight-tracking data and speculation until investigators and rescuers establish them.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Debris field found off Nantucket from missing medical plane
seoDescription: Searchers found a debris field linked to a Canadian-registered medical plane that vanished off Nantucket with six people aboard.
